**MEMO**

**To:** All Employees
**From:** [Name / Title]
**Date:** [Date]
**Subject:** Updated Remote Work Policy, Effective February 1

---

**Overview**

We're updating our remote work policy to give everyone clear, consistent expectations while preserving the flexibility that matters to our team. The new policy takes effect **February 1**.

**What's Changing**

**1. Remote work allowance**
Employees may work remotely up to **3 days per week**. The remaining days are expected to be in the office. Your manager will work with you to settle on a schedule that fits your role and your team's needs.

**2. Core hours**
All employees are expected to be available during core hours, **10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Eastern**, regardless of work location or time zone. Outside these hours, you have flexibility to structure your day as long as your work gets done. Meetings and team collaboration should be scheduled within core hours whenever possible.

**3. Meal stipend for Tuesday and Thursday office days**
To encourage in-person collaboration, employees who work from the office on **Tuesdays and Thursdays** will receive a meal stipend for those days. [Insert amount and how it's claimed, e.g., expense submission or payroll.]

**Requesting an Exception**

We recognize that some situations won't fit neatly within this policy, such as medical needs, caregiving responsibilities, relocation, or role-specific requirements. To request an exception:

1. **Submit a written request** to your manager describing the arrangement you're requesting, the reason, and the intended duration.
2. **Manager review:** Your manager will review the request and forward it with their recommendation to [HR contact / People Operations] within [5] business days.
3. **Decision:** [HR / Leadership] will respond in writing within [10] business days of receiving the request.
4. **Review period:** Approved exceptions will be documented and revisited periodically, typically every [6] months, or sooner if circumstances change.

Requests related to medical conditions or disabilities will be handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable law. You may contact [HR contact] directly if you prefer not to go through your manager.

**Timeline**

- **Now through January 31:** Current arrangements remain in place. Please discuss your planned schedule with your manager.
- **February 1:** The new policy takes effect.

**Questions**

If you have questions about the policy, please reach out to your manager or [HR contact / email]. We'll also hold [a Q&A session on date, if applicable] to address anything that's unclear.

Thank you for your continued flexibility and commitment as we make this transition.

[Name]
[Title]

---

**Notes for you to fill in:** the sender and date, the stipend amount and claim process, the exception-request contacts and turnaround times, and whether to hold a Q&A session. I also assumed that current arrangements stay in place until February 1. Adjust that if it's not accurate.

# Memo: Updated Remote Work Policy, Effective February 1, 2027

**To:** All employees
**From:** [Name, Title]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Remote work policy update

---

## Summary

Starting **Monday, February 1, 2027**, we're updating our remote work policy to give everyone a predictable structure. The policy has three parts:

- You may work remotely **up to 3 days per week**.
- Everyone is available during **core hours, 10:00 am to 3:00 pm Eastern**.
- Anyone in the office on **Tuesdays and Thursdays** receives a **meal stipend**.

We want to keep the flexibility that works well for us. We also want to make sure we have enough shared time, both in person and online, to collaborate, mentor each other, and move quickly.

## What's changing

### 1. Remote work: up to 3 days per week
- You can work remotely up to three days in a typical work week. In practice, that means being in the office at least two days a week.
- Each team will agree on a consistent weekly pattern so people know when to expect colleagues in the office. Managers will confirm those patterns by **[date, e.g., January 15]**.
- Remote work means working from a location with a reliable internet connection where you can do your job effectively and securely. Remote work from outside your home state or country can have tax, legal, and insurance implications. Please talk to [HR contact] before working from another location for an extended period.

### 2. Core hours: 10:00 am to 3:00 pm Eastern
- Everyone should be available and responsive during core hours, whether in the office or remote. This applies regardless of your time zone.
- Please schedule meetings within core hours whenever possible.
- Outside core hours, you have flexibility in when you start and finish, as long as you meet your role's expectations and your total hours. Please agree on any regular pattern with your manager.
- Occasional personal needs, like appointments or school pickups, are fine. Give your team notice when you can.

### 3. Tuesday/Thursday office meal stipend
- Employees who work from the office on a Tuesday or Thursday receive a meal stipend of **[$ amount]** per day.
- To claim it, **[describe process, e.g., submit the receipt through the expense tool by the end of the following week / badge-in verification applies automatically]**.
- The stipend is for a meal on the day you're in the office. It's [taxable / non-taxable per our accountant's guidance, confirm before sending].
- We chose Tuesdays and Thursdays to make sure plenty of people overlap in person. This is an incentive, not a requirement. If those days don't work for your schedule, you can still be in the office on other days and fit within the policy.

## Requesting an exception

We know one policy won't fit every situation. Examples include a medical condition, a disability, caregiving responsibilities, a long commute or relocation, or a role that needs a different arrangement. You can ask for an exception.

**How to request one:**
1. **Talk to your manager first.** Explain what you're asking for, such as a different number of remote days, a modified core-hours window, or a temporary arrangement.
2. **Submit a written request** to [HR contact / email / form link] with:
   - What you're requesting (specific days, hours, or schedule)
   - Whether it's temporary (with start and end dates) or ongoing
   - The reason, to the extent you're comfortable sharing, and how you'll keep your work and collaboration on track
   - Your manager's recommendation, if you have it
3. **Review.** [HR contact] and your manager will review the request together. We aim to respond **within [10] business days**. If your situation is urgent, say so in the request and we'll move faster.
4. **Decision.** You'll receive a written decision. If we can't approve the request as submitted, we'll explain why and try to find an alternative that works.

**Good to know:**
- Requests based on a medical condition, disability, or religious practice are handled as accommodation requests under applicable law. Please contact [HR contact] directly. You don't have to go through your manager first, and your information will be kept confidential.
- Approved exceptions are documented and reviewed every [6 months] or when your circumstances change.
- Exceptions are decided on the needs of the role and the business. They are not a judgment of your performance.
- Requests made before February 1 will be considered and answered before the policy takes effect, wherever possible. We encourage you to submit them by **[January 8]**.

## Timeline

| Date | What happens |
|---|---|
| [Today's date] | Policy announced |
| [Date] | Q&A session with leadership ([time, location/link]) |
| [January 8] | Suggested deadline for exception requests, so we can respond before launch |
| [January 15] | Teams confirm weekly in-office patterns |
| **February 1, 2027** | **Policy takes effect** |
| [May 1] | We'll check in on how the policy is working and gather feedback |

## Questions

Please bring questions to your manager or to [HR contact, email]. We'll also hold a Q&A session on [date], and we'll keep an FAQ at [location] and update it as questions come in.

We'll review this policy after the first few months and adjust it based on your feedback and how it works in practice. Thank you for helping us make it work.

[Name]
[Title]

---

**MEMO**

**To:** All Employees
**From:** [Sender name/title]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Updated Remote Work Policy, Effective February 1, 2027

---

**The bottom line**

Starting February 1, 2027, you may work remotely up to **3 days per week**. Core hours are **10am to 3pm Eastern**. If you're in the office on **Tuesdays and Thursdays**, you'll receive a **meal stipend**.

**How it works**

**The 3-day limit.** Each week, you can work remotely up to 3 days. The remaining days are in-office days. In a week with a company holiday or PTO, those days don't count as remote days. For example, if you take Friday off as PTO, you still have up to 3 remote days among the days you work. Remote days don't carry over from one week to the next.

**Core hours.** Between 10am and 3pm Eastern, be available and responsive. That means you're reachable on chat and email, you can hop on a call or join meetings, and you reply promptly to teammates. Outside that window, you can set your schedule in agreement with your manager. Core hours apply whether you're home or in the office.

**Meal stipend.** Come into the office on a Tuesday or Thursday and you earn a stipend of **$[amount]** for that day. It's earned per day, so each Tuesday or Thursday you're in the office counts. Submit your stipend through the usual expense process. If you work remotely on those days, there's no stipend for that day.

**Requesting an exception**

We know some situations don't fit neatly into the policy, such as a medical need, a caregiving responsibility, a temporary move, or a role with different requirements. If that's you, please ask.

- **Who to ask:** Send your request to **[contact name]**, with your manager copied.
- **What to include:** Describe what you're asking for (for example, more remote days, a different set of core hours, or a different in-office schedule), why you need it, how long you need it for, and how you'll keep your work and your team's collaboration on track.
- **When to expect an answer:** You'll hear back within 5 business days. If we need more information, we'll let you know within that time.

Exceptions are reviewed case by case, and requests are kept confidential.

**Questions?**

Reach out to your manager or [contact name] anytime. We want this policy to give you flexibility while keeping us connected as a team. Thank you for all you do.
